hints: When the particle reaches its greatest height, its vertical velocity is zero ($v = 0$).
From the point at height $0.5\text{ m}$ where speed is $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, use $v^2 = u^2 - 2gs_1$ to find the extra height $s_1$ gained.
Add $0.5\text{ m}$ to $s_1$ to find the total height above $O$.
walkthrough: At the greatest height, the upward velocity of the particle is instantaneously zero ($v = 0$).
Consider the motion from height $0.5\text{ m}$ to the maximum height. The initial velocity is $u = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and acceleration is $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Use the velocity-displacement relation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$:
$$0 = 6^2 + 2(-10)s_1$$
$$0 = 36 - 20s_1$$
$$20s_1 = 36 \implies s_1 = \frac{36}{20} = 1.8\text{ m}$$

Add the height already gained above $O$ ($0.5\text{ m}$) to find the total greatest height:
$$H = 0.5 + 1.8 = 2.3\text{ m}$$

hints: Find the time taken to fall from rest at the maximum height ($H = 2.3\text{ m}$) back to $O$ using $s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
By symmetry of motion under gravity, the time of flight upwards from $O$ to maximum height equals the time of flight downwards from maximum height to $O$.
Multiply the single descent time by 2 to obtain the total time of flight.
walkthrough:
By symmetry of projectile motion under constant gravitational acceleration with no air resistance, the time taken to rise from $O$ to the maximum height equals the time taken to fall from the maximum height back to $O$:
$$t_{\text{up}} = t_{\text{down}}$$

Calculate the time of descent from the peak ($H = 2.3\text{ m}$) from rest ($u = 0$) under gravity $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$$
$$2.3 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(10)t_{\text{down}}^2 = 5t_{\text{down}}^2$$

Divide by $5$ to solve for $t_{\text{down}}^2$:
$$t_{\text{down}}^2 = \frac{2.3}{5} = 0.46$$
$$t_{\text{down}} = \sqrt{0.46} \approx 0.67823\text{ s}$$

Calculate the total flight time by doubling $t_{\text{down}}$:
$$t_{\text{total}} = 2 \times t_{\text{down}} = 2 \times 0.67823 \approx 1.356\text{ s} \approx 1.36\text{ s}$$
